trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (plain mean of full pool) and the runner-up is statistically indistinguishable (margin 0.00172). The diagnosis explicitly warns that the series is close to noise and fitted weights would overfit, the ranking is unstable, and subsets all performed worse. This is a clear case to accept the leader.

action_args.justification: The series has strong trend and seasonality but low predictability and ambiguous stationarity, making it close to noise. The model ranking is highly unstable (Kendall tau 0.049) with correlated error groups, so no subset or fitted weighting can reliably outperform a simple mean of the full pool. All subset-based strategies (pool1/2/3) and robust alternatives (median, trimmed mean) scored worse than the plain mean. The leader is a seed baseline and the runner-up is statistically indistinguishable, confirming that the full-pool mean is the most robust combination for this noisy, unstable-ranking series.
